snippet.title: Automations in Jira with Cursor | Atlassian
snippet.description:
What if every incoming issue could trigger Cursor Agent automatically? With agent automations in Jira, you set a condition, like a specific summary prefix for security issues or improvement requests, and when a matching ticket lands, your chosen coding agent (Jira Coding Agent, Claude, or Cursor) picks it up and gets to work. No manual triage, no delay. Set it once, and your agents do the rest. Watch to see how to wire up agent automations in Jira step by step.

🔗 Learn more about Jira AI features: https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira

snippet.description:

From the difference between prediction and reasoning, to the growing problem of AI sprawl, to why change management might matter more than the technology itself — this is a must-watch for anyone trying to make sense of AI in their organization.

snippet.title: Agentic Pipelines | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Most CI/CD pipelines are fragile bash scripts that break when things change. What if your pipeline could think?

Agentic Pipelines lets you add AI agents as steps in Bitbucket Pipelines. In this video, I show an agent that reads a design spec from Confluence, generates frontend code, runs tests, and opens a PR, all inside a pipeline.

With Agentic Pipelines, Bitbucket goes from a CI/CD platform to a full workflow and automation engine you can use far beyond builds and deploys.

Learn more about Bitbucket Agentic Pipelines here: https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/agentic-pipelines/

snippet.title: How KFC Uses AI Agents to Ship Software Faster | Atlassian Rovo
snippet.description:
KFC's engineering teams were drowning in release admin — chasing people for risk assessments, impact details, and component info. Not anymore. Now their custom Change Agent (built with Atlassian Rovo) pulls up everything teams need against a release — risk, impact, associated components — instantly.

The result? Massively reduced admin time, engineers doing what they love, and a culture shift from "who do I ask?" to "I can find it myself."

Read the full KFC × Atlassian story: https://www.atlassian.com/customers/kfc

snippet.title: Tracking deliverables in Jira as a Product Manager | How I Atlassian
snippet.description:
Tired of being your team's "status bot"? In this video, a Product Manager shares how she stopped chasing updates over DMs and started using Jira to keep her team aligned, so she can focus on what actually matters.

Here's what you'll learn:
✅ How to centralize launch tasks in Jira as work items
✅ How to organize your backlog and pull priorities into sprints
✅ How to use work item comments so your team self-reports progress

Whether you're new to Jira or just looking for a better way to manage deliverables, this workflow will help you reclaim your time and reduce the chaos.

snippet.title: How Rovo helps finance close the books faster | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Managing financial systems at scale is complex. Multiple SaaS applications, ERP integrations, transaction flows, and month-end close activities must work seamlessly to ensure data integrity and reporting accuracy.

In this video, Alex Auerbach, on the Finance AI and Enablement team at Atlassian, shares how they built Finance360, a Rovo agent that delivers real-time monitoring, proactive alerts, and intelligent troubleshooting across critical financial systems.

By combining Jira, Confluence, Slack, automation, and the Finance360 Rovo agent:

Reduces manual operational effort from hours to minutes

Monitors job runs, transactions, and integrations 24/7

Sends Slack-based summaries and real-time system insights

Assists with error resolution and period-end close

Rovo turns fragmented monitoring into a unified, AI-powered command center — helping teams shift from reactive firefighting to proactive control.

snippet.title: Kraken: From knowledge to action with Rovo Skills | Team '26 | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Rovo Skills, agents, and automation can turn hours of manual work into seconds and Kraken's 30,000 monthly executions prove it's already working.

In this Team '26 session, Atlassian and Kraken show how any team can encode their custom workflows into reusable Rovo Skills, compose them into agents, and automate them end-to-end — all powered by the Atlassian Teamwork Graph.

From security question resolution dropping from 4 hours to 12 minutes, to
faster performance review cycles, see what's possible when AI learns how your team actually works.

Key takeaways:
• Build a repeatable playbook: identify painful workflows, encode them into
  Rovo Skills, and give your whole team the same superpower.
• See Rovo Skills in action across three surfaces: Chat, Agents, and
  Automations — from manual trigger to fully autonomous workflow.
• Hear how Kraken uses Rovo Skills across security, knowledge management,
  and performance reviews — with real metrics to back it up.

Speakers:
• Josh Devenny, Distinguished Product Manager, Atlassian
• Ted Moskalenko, Head of AI Enablement, Kraken

snippet.title: How one PM scaled customer discovery with AI
snippet.description:
Customer interviews are one of the most powerful ways to build better products — but they’re also time-consuming.

In this video, Avinoam “Avi” Zelenko, Principal Product Manager at Atlassian, shares how he transformed the way he runs customer interviews using AI automation and Rovo agents.

What used to take hours of coordination, note-taking, and manual summaries now happens automatically. By stitching together the Teamwork Collection and Slack, Avi built a workflow that captures conversations, summarizes insights, and shares them across teams in real time.

The result?
He scaled from just 2 customer calls per month to nearly 200 calls in three months — without increasing manual effort.

More importantly, customers feel heard. Teams gain shared understanding. And product decisions are grounded in real insight, not guesswork.

Want to read more about Avi’s process? Check out this blog for the full story: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/artificial-intelligence/customer-insights-rovo-agent

Learn more about Rovo: https://www.atlassian.com/software/rovo

snippet.title: New Pipeline Triggers | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Bitbucket Pipelines already supports triggering on repository pushes and pull request pushes. But if you wanted to react to other events like a deployment finishing, a build failing, or a PR getting merged, you had to wire that up yourself with webhooks or external glue code.

New trigger types let you define those conditions directly in your YAML. You can fire custom pipelines on events like pipeline-completed, deployment-completed, pullrequest-created, pullrequest-fulfilled, and more.

In this video, we walk through how to set up these triggers in your bitbucket-pipelines.yml file so you can chain stages together, send notifications on failures, or generate release notes on merge without building external orchestration.

Learn more about new Bitbucket Pipelines trigger types: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/new-triggers-for-pipeline-deployment-and-pull-request-events

snippet.description:
In the Startup Stories with Atlassian series, we interview founders about their entrepreneurial journey, learn about the problems they are trying to solve, and explore how their teams are using Atlassian tools to grow and deliver value to their customers.

In this episode of Startup Stories with Atlassian, Adam sits down with Thiago, Co-Founder of Dooor, to explore how his team merges AI capabilities with Atlassian tools to go from ideation to feature prototype in just 10 days, without burning out the team.

Thiago shares Dooor's journey of transforming traditional project management into an AI-powered workflow, how they integrate AI with Jira for automated updates, and why finding the balance between AI-driven speed and human capabilities is the real unlock for early-stage teams.

- How Dooor builds from ideation to feature prototype in 10 days using AI + Atlassian
- Integrating AI with Jira for automated updates – staying organized while moving fast
- Using Loom for transparent weekly updates that reduce micromanagement
- Finding the sweet spot between AI-driven speed and avoiding team burnout

snippet.description:

How to build credibility and attract talent as a solo founder with no funding

Why adopting Jira and Atlassian tools early is a recruiting signal – not just a tooling decision

What to look for in early hires: grit over pedigree, and ownership as the unlock

Why collaboration tools can't wait until after funding

snippet.title: How Tasteport Turned a Family Pain Point into a Scalable Platform | Atlassian for Startups
snippet.description:
In the Startup Stories with Atlassian series, we interview founders about their entrepreneurial journey, learn about the problems they are trying to solve, and explore how their teams are using Atlassian tools to grow and deliver value to their customers.

In this episode of Startup Stories with Atlassian, Adam sits down with Aaqib Usmani, Founder & CEO of Tasteport, to explore how he's building the multicultural grocery infrastructure powering a $280B specialty market – and why the right internal tools are just as important as the product itself.

Aaqib shares how a personal frustration with finding authentic ethnic groceries in Toronto turned into a multi-platform logistics company serving 15 cities across the Greater Toronto Area. Learn how Tasteport uses AI to transform messy grocer spreadsheets into shoppable catalogs, coordinates five interconnected platforms with a distributed team, and why they went all-in on Atlassian from day one.

🔑 What you'll learn:

Using AI to solve real operational problems – turning chaotic inventory files into clean online catalogs in minutes

Why Jira sits at the center of managing work across five connected platforms

How the Atlassian for Startups program enabled enterprise-grade tooling from the start

What's next: Rovo, AI agents, and MCP capabilities on their engineering roadmap

snippet.title: How California's DHCS aligns strategy and delivery with Strategy Collection | Team '26 | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Learn how the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) moved from siloed work to a connected, enterprise-wide operating model using the Atlassian Strategy Collection.

As one of the largest public health organizations in the United States, DHCS needed a way to unify idea management, goal alignment, and execution visibility. Discover how integrating strategy and work management can improve transparency, accountability, and decision-making across every layer of a complex organization.

snippet.title: Variable Sharing and Dynamic Step Conditions | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Bitbucket Pipelines lets you invoke child pipelines from a parent step, but until now there was no way to pass information between them. Variable sharing changes that.

You can define variables in a parent step and pass them directly to child pipelines as custom pipeline variables. With dynamic step conditions, those child pipelines can make decisions at runtime based on the values they receive, like skipping a deployment when a security scan detects critical vulnerabilities.

In this video, we walk through how to add variable sharing and dynamic step conditions to a Bitbucket Pipeline so you can build modular pipelines that react to information only available at runtime.

Learn more about variable sharing here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/unlocking-workflow-flexibility-with-variable-sharing-between-parent-and-child-pipelines

Learn more about dynamic step conditions here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/introducing-dynamic-step-condition-for-bitbucket-pipelines

snippet.title: Crystal Widjaja: Why PMs Must Get Comfortable with the CLI
snippet.description:
Crystal Widjaja (former Chief Product Officer at Gojek and Reforge instructor) has built data and growth systems at an incredible scale. While many product managers are stuck using AI for surface-level summaries and "one-shot" artifacts, Crystal has spent her "semi-retirement" architecting a sophisticated AI agent harness that manages everything from her daily prep to maintaining a "friendship CRM."In this episode, Crystal pulls back the curtain on the messy practical reality of her technical stack—built with Obsidian, Python, and Claude Code—to demonstrate how PMs can move past the "trap" of abstracted GUI tools and start building infrastructure that truly scales their impact.We discuss

The shift from surface-level prompting to building mature agent infrastructure and "context engineering"

Automating low-leverage work like meeting notes and status updates so you can focus on creative strategy and customer interaction

The unique AI advantage in Southeast Asia: How a culture of delegation has prepared leaders for the age of agents

Three things that won't change: Vision setting, creative voice, and deep customer empathy

The "Ralph Loop" framework: Chaining complex AI tasks together for autonomous execution

Key takeaways

PMs must get comfortable with the CLI. Crystal argues that relying solely on simplified AI interfaces is a "trap" that prevents you from understanding the underlying system. To truly improve your workflow and leverage AI's full power, you need to be willing to open the terminal and interact with the technical scaffolding yourself.

Context is the new prompt engineering. The first wave of AI was about learning how to prompt; the next wave is about "context engineering." Quality output depends on the data you feed the system, from meeting transcripts to project files, and building the pipelines to sync that context automatically.

Focus on the smallest unit of work first. Rather than aiming for "big bang" AI solutions, start by automating one specific task you hate, such as syncing meeting notes to your computer. Once that works, iterate and chain those units together into a more comprehensive agent harness.

AI should enhance your humanity, not just your productivity. Crystal uses her AI chief of staff to maintain a "friendship CRM," tracking details like a friend's past mention of a marathon or gift ideas. By offloading the "menial" memory work to AI, she frees up mental energy to be a more present and thoughtful friend.

Adopt a "semi-unemployed" mindset. The best way to stay relevant in the AI era is to create enough space in your schedule to play with new tools. By automating low-leverage tasks, you gain the time needed to stay ahead of the "AI overlords" and master the evolving landscape of agent orchestration.

snippet.title: Teamwork Collection: Built for the Next Era of Teamwork
snippet.description:
Your team's best ideas shouldn't get lost between the doc, the ticket, and the meeting recording — but that's exactly what happens when AI lives outside your workflow.

Teamwork Collection by Atlassian puts AI agents and your team on the same page — literally. Ideas flow to execution, agents pull context from your actual projects, and the line between "human work" and "AI work" starts to disappear.

Built on the Teamwork Graph, Teamwork Collection connects Jira, Confluence, Loom, and Rovo so agents understand what's happening across your work. Assign agents to Jira tasks, @mention them on Confluence pages, or brief them with a Loom recording. They act with full context, full accountability, and full audit trails.

No more toggling between six tabs or copy-pasting context into a chatbot. Ship faster, stay aligned, and let agents handle the work that slows your team down.

snippet.title: Team '26 Highlight: Agents in Jira
snippet.description:
Jira is shifting from work tracking to work orchestration. In this clip from the Team '26 Founder Keynote, Atlassian co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes and Sherif Mansour, Head of AI, show how AI agents now work alongside your team directly inside Jira.

You can now:
• Assign work items to first-party Rovo agents or third-party agents from partners like GitHub Copilot, Canva, Figma, Cursor, and more
• @mention agents in comments for in-context help
• Embed agents into workflow statuses so they're automatically triggered when work moves forward
• Every action is logged with full audit trails — you stay in control the whole time

Agents in Jira is generally available now for all Jira customers with Rovo.

Learn more and explore the full Jira Spring 2026 Release → https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/release

Recorded live at Team '26, Anaheim, May 2026.

snippet.title: AI keynote – Building AI‑native teams with Atlassian Rovo | Team '26 | Atlassian
snippet.description:
AI shouldn’t just support individuals. It should actively move work forward for teams and organizations.

In this keynote, we’ll show how Rovo, powered by the Teamwork Graph, understands your business end to end – who’s working on what, where knowledge lives, and how work flows across teams. With that context, Rovo doesn’t just surface answers, it takes action.

Through live demos and real-world examples of human-AI collaboration, you’ll see how teams set intent while Rovo orchestrates multi-step workflows across Jira, Confluence, and your favorite SaaS apps, while respecting existing permissions, governance, and compliance.

You’ll leave with a clear understanding of how Rovo fits into everyday work to speed decisions, reduce busywork, and help teams operate as truly AI-native.

snippet.title: Highlights: Where does your chain break? Strategy that lives in boardrooms and PowerPoints
snippet.description:
Stop losing millions to disconnected work. Learn how to build a unified system of work using the Atlassian stack to align engineering execution with executive strategy.

When engineering teams lack a unified system, they often chase the wrong priorities or duplicate efforts, leading to execution drift and lower morale. In this session, Natalia Baryshnikova (Atlassian) and Vince Butera (Anaplan) share how to move beyond a collection of tools to create a single, connected platform using Jira, Jira Align, Compass, Confluence, and Rovo.

Discover how rooting your engineering operations in strategic clarity and technical truth reduces toil for developers while providing leadership with the visibility they need to forecast with confidence.

snippet.title: Designing for the beautiful mess of modern work | Team '26 | Atlassian
snippet.description:
"Teamwork is messy – and AI might make it even messier. Learn how the Chief Design Officers of Atlassian and Figma are designing for that reality to turn friction into a creative edge.

The best ideas often come from false starts, conflicting opinions, and rapid iteration. In this session, Charlie Sutton (Atlassian) and Loredana Crisan (Figma) discuss why design shouldn’t eliminate the ""mess"" of collaboration, but rather the friction surrounding it – like busywork, duplicate effort, and tool sprawl.

Discover how Atlassian and Figma are building human+AI experiences rooted in the Teamwork Graph to protect human agency. Learn how thoughtful design can empower your team to move faster, decide better, and build work they’re truly proud of.

localized.title: Bring the power of AI agents to your Jira workflows | Team '26 | Atlassian
localized.description:
Most teams have experimented with AI, but few have made agents true teammates in their daily workflows. Jira is changing that. By serving as an agent orchestration hub, Jira now allows your teams to bring AI agents directly into the work they are already doing – without the need for new tools or extra processes.

Join Matthew Canham (Principal Product Manager, AI) and Natalie Chung (Senior Group Product Manager, Jira) as they explore the evolution of Jira. Learn how to assign work to agents, blend human and automated execution, and manage critical factors like trust, permissions, and autonomy. You’ll also hear ""can’t-miss"" lessons from early adopters on what is possible when integrating third-party agents into your Jira environment.

snippet.title: Rovo: AI-native teamwork, powered by your organization's context | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Your team's best work starts with having the full picture. Meet Rovo — Atlassian's AI that understands your people, projects, decisions, and code to power answers and actions that help teams ship faster, decide smarter, and scale with trust. 

🔍 Deep context - Rovo is powered by Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph, our intelligent data layer that maps relationships across your work, projects, code, people, decisions, and even history of work across all your Atlassian apps like Jira and Confluence, and connected tools. This allows Rovo to not just read your Jira epics and work items, but also similar work items, related docs, and past decisions so you’re always acting with the full picture.

⚡ Workflow orchestration - Agents keep your workflows moving, handling next steps, and keeping everything on track. Assign agents to review code, draft release notes, or even onboard new hires, @mention them in comments for in-context help, or add them directly into Jira workflows to handle next steps automatically. With MCP Gallery, agents can connect to tools like Figma, Amplitude, HubSpot, Canva, Intercom, and more - pulling live data and taking action across your entire stack.

✨ Built for teams - We’ve built Rovo to be collaborative, proactive, transparent, and dare we say, joyful to use. Rovo works across your Atlassian apps and connected SaaS tools, chat, desktop, and mobile - meeting you wherever work happens. It's designed to feel like a natural extension of your team, not another tool to learn.

🔒 Enterprise-ready — You already trust Atlassian with your most important workflows, and Rovo is no different. It’s built with the same security, privacy, governance, and compliance features that we build into our Cloud platform. Permission-aware actions, data residency options, and admin controls so your team can adopt AI at scale and with confidence.

Learn more about Rovo: www.atlassian.com/software/rovo

Your team's best work starts with having the full picture. Meet Rovo — Atlassian's AI that understands your people, projects, decisions, and code to power answers and actions that help teams ship faster, decide smarter, and scale with trust. 

🔍 Deep context - Rovo is powered by Atlassian’s Teamwork Graph, our intelligent data layer that maps relationships across your work, projects, code, people, decisions, and even history of work across all your Atlassian apps like Jira and Confluence, and connected tools. This allows Rovo to not just read your Jira epics and work items, but also similar work items, related docs, and past decisions so you’re always acting with the full picture.

⚡ Workflow orchestration - Agents keep your workflows moving, handling next steps, and keeping everything on track. Assign agents to review code, draft release notes, or even onboard new hires, @mention them in comments for in-context help, or add them directly into Jira workflows to handle next steps automatically. With MCP Gallery, agents can connect to tools like Figma, Amplitude, HubSpot, Canva, Intercom, and more - pulling live data and taking action across your entire stack.

✨ Built for teams - We’ve built Rovo to be collaborative, proactive, transparent, and dare we say, joyful to use. Rovo works across your Atlassian apps and connected SaaS tools, chat, desktop, and mobile - meeting you wherever work happens. It's designed to feel like a natural extension of your team, not another tool to learn.

🔒 Enterprise-ready — You already trust Atlassian with your most important workflows, and Rovo is no different. It’s built with the same security, privacy, governance, and compliance features that we build into our Cloud platform. Permission-aware actions, data residency options, and admin controls so your team can adopt AI at scale and with confidence.

Learn more about Rovo: www.atlassian.com/software/rovo

snippet.title: Getting started building in Rovo Studio | Atlassian
snippet.description:
New to Atlassian Studio?

This video walks you through exactly what a first session looks like — from landing page to finished build in just a few minutes.

We follow a team lead who wants to stop being the onboarding bottleneck for new starters in their team. Instead of answering the same questions on repeat, they describe the problem to Studio, and Studio builds an onboarding agent that new starters can ask instead. You'll see how Studio starts with solution plans and then helps you build, all without any code.

And if you're ever unsure what to type, just ask. Studio is designed to help you through it. Whether you prefer to build with AI guidance or get hands-on manually, everything you create lives in Studio — ready to edit, share, or build on.

snippet.title: What you can build in Rovo Studio | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Atlassian Studio builds three things that work inside the products your team already uses — and this video explains each one.

- Agents are AI assistants you build for your team. They live in Confluence, Jira, or your service desk, answer questions, guide people through processes, and take action on their behalf, like booking intro meetings for a new starter using their calendar and messaging tools. 
- Automation flows handle the repetitive work you do manually every week. Set them once, and they keep running: chasing, reminding, routing so you don't have to. 
- Apps extend your Atlassian products directly. Not a new tool to open, but something that lives inside Jira, Confluence, or JSM, built exactly for how your team works.

You don't need to know which one you need before you start. Describe the problem to Studio, and it'll figure out what to build.

snippet.title: Share artifacts between parent and child pipelines | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Bitbucket Pipelines lets you build reusable pipelines and share them across repositories.

These reusable, shared pipelines need a way to share artifacts.

Otherwise, we’ll have to repeat expensive steps such as downloading and installing dependencies and building the application code.

You can now specify an artifacts section for child pipelines, with upload and download keywords.

Artifacts listed under upload will be moved from the parent pipeline into the child pipeline, where they can be used and potentially modified.

Artifacts listed under download will be moved from the child pipeline, up a level, to the calling parent pipeline, where they can be used and potentially passed to other child pipelines.

In this way, a parent pipeline could download artifacts from a build child pipeline and then upload them to a testing child pipeline.

Learn more about sharing artifacts between parent and child pipelines here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/share-artifacts-between-parent-and-child-pipelines

snippet.title: Split your Bitbucket Pipelines workflows across multiple files | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Building and maintaining a 2000+ line bitbucket-pipelines.yml can be a lot of work. Now you can split large bitbucket-pipelines.yml files into multiple, smaller pipelines.yml files.

These smaller files can be composed via shared pipeline syntax to replicate the functionality of the original bitbucket-pipelines.yml file. They can also be shared with and reused in other repositories.

You can learn more about multiple pipelines.yml files here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/split-your-pipelines-workflows-across-multiple-files

snippet.title: Rovo Dev for learning | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Join Jovana, a Senior Technical Evangelist at Atlassian, and Nick, a Senior Systems Engineer at Atlassian, as they demonstrate how Rovo Dev can be used to accelerate technical learning and automate complex engineering tasks.

Key Highlights:
- Accelerated Learning and Onboarding: Nick demonstrates how he used Rovo Dev to quickly get up to speed on a new technology stack (Kubernetes) when transitioning between teams at Atlassian.
- Automated Infrastructure Setup: The demo shows Rovo Dev checking for required local tools, recommending a setup method (using "kind"), and generating scripts to create and clean up a multi-node Kubernetes cluster on a laptop.
- Application Deployment and Scaling: Nick uses Rovo Dev to create a Python web application from scratch, deploy it to the cluster, and then scale the application to five replicas.
- Automated Documentation: The video showcases Rovo Dev's ability to integrate with Confluence to automatically generate a comprehensive guide detailing all the setup steps and learning exercises completed during the session.

snippet.title: Run with Rovo Dev in bulk | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
In this video, we show how Rovo Dev lets you run multiple AI coding sessions in parallel, so a whole batch of Jira issues can move forward while you work on something else:

- Start with a single Jira issue: generate code with Rovo Dev, let it pull in Confluence specs, and explore the repo
- Watch it write production-quality code across multiple files, run tests, debug failures, and open a draft PR
- Then switch to bulk mode: select 7+ Jira issues and trigger “Generate code with Rovo Dev” in one go
- Configure all sessions in bulk (same settings, applied once), then fire them off
- See independent cloud sessions run in parallel – each gathering its own context, writing its own fix, running tests, and opening its own PR

7 tickets. Zero context switching.

This is Run with Rovo Dev in Bulk: scale your impact by letting the agent handle the repetitive work across your entire backlog.

snippet.title: Rovo Dev code review in GitHub | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Ship safer code faster with Rovo Dev Code Reviewer, fully integrated into your GitHub pull requests.

In this video, we’ll show you how Rovo Dev automatically reviews every PR against your team’s standards, not some generic checklist. Using a simple config file, you can teach Rovo Dev exactly what “good” looks like in your repo.

What you’ll see in this demo:
How to configure review-agent.md file with:
- Security rules (e.g., exposed credentials, missing input validation)
- Performance expectations (like acceptable query response times)
- Documentation rules (e.g., every public method needs a docstring)
-Team-specific coding conventions

How Rovo Dev automatically:
- Triggers on each GitHub commit to a pull request
- Scans code changes for security vulnerabilities and performance issues
- Checks your code against the rules in review-agent.md file
- Flags potential bugs and logic errors

What the review looks like in GitHub:
- Inline comments right next to the relevant lines of code
- Explanations of what’s wrong, why it matters, and how to fix it
- Reviews tailored to your security & compliance needs 

If your team cares about security, compliance, and quality in production systems, this workflow shows how Rovo Dev can help you enforce those standards on every PR, automatically.

snippet.title: Automate code generation with Rovo Dev | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Security vulnerabilities pile up. Your team doesn't have time to fix them fast enough.

What if the fix happened automatically, the moment the ticket was created?

In this video, we show how to combine Jira Automation with Rovo Dev to create a fully hands-off vulnerability remediation pipeline:
- Set up a Jira automation rule that triggers Rovo Dev the instant a vulnerability ticket is created or labeled
- Watch Rovo Dev read the vulnerability description, scan the codebase to find the affected code, and check your team's review agent file for security standards and fix patterns
- It writes a context-aware fix - not a generic patch, but one that understands your codebase and your security requirements
- Rovo Dev runs the test suite, and if anything fails, it debugs and iterates automatically until everything is green
- It opens a draft PR, ready for human review, all while the developer was doing something else entirely

Raise the tickets, walk away, come back to PRs.
This is automated code generation with Rovo Dev: turn Jira Automation into your always-on security engineer.

snippet.title: Generate requirements, epics & diagrams with Rovo Dev | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Turn messy brainstorming notes into production-ready plans in minutes.

In this video, we show how Rovo Dev transforms a rough Confluence page into a complete delivery pack:
- Reads a Confluence brainstorming page and auto-generates a clean, structured requirements document
- Enriches its own context using the Atlassian Teamwork Graph, pulling in related Jira issues, relevant code, and other docs
- Saves the requirements back into Confluence for the whole team
- Generates a Jira epic with child stories, each with detailed acceptance criteria and user journeys
- Produces architecture and sequence diagrams directly from the requirements

From a messy brainstorm to a fully structured backlog and diagrams, in seconds, not hours.

This is document generation with Rovo Dev: beyond code, into complete, living documentation for your team.

snippet.title: Rovo Dev for platform engineers | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Jovana, a Senior Technical Evangelist at Atlassian, sits down with Victor, a Platform Engineer on the Atlassian cloud infrastructure team, to discuss the real impact of using Rovo Dev in Victor’s day-to-day.

Victor shares how his team leveraged Rovo Dev to overcome a significant challenge in GCP cloud resource emulation, transforming a process that would have taken weeks into one that took only a few hours.

What You'll Learn:
- Rovo Dev as a Coding Assistant: See how Victor used Rovo Dev to analyze existing open-source code patterns and automatically generate new emulated resources, such as service accounts and secret managers.
- Real results: Learn how using Rovo Dev replaced creating thousands of real GCP resources with fast, local memory-based emulation, dramatically cutting cloud costs and shrinking end-to-end test time from 20 minutes to just 5 seconds.
- Beyond Coding: Victor discusses how he uses Rovo Dev to analyze customer support trends in Slack, identify friction areas, and improve documentation and onboarding.
- Pro-Tip for Rovo Dev: Discover why providing the right context is like onboarding a new team member and is the key to getting the most out of your AI tools.

snippet.title: Rovo Dev for tech leaders | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Join Jovana, a Senior Technical Evangelist at Atlassian, and Matt, a Senior Engineering Manager and the lead behind Rovo Dev for Jira, as they discuss how Atlassian Rovo is changing the way engineering teams manage tasks and distractions.

In this video, Matt demonstrates how Rovo Dev can help engineering managers shield their teams from time-consuming interruptions by automating routine tasks directly within Jira.

Key Highlights:
- Autonomous work in the cloud: Rovo Dev operates within a secure cloud sandbox, enabling multiple agents to work behind the scenes simultaneously without requiring local resources.
- Shielding your team: Managers can use Rovo Dev to handle urgent but distracting requests, such as security vulnerabilities or engineering health tickets, keeping their team focused on high-priority projects.
- Scale with automation: Learn how to set up Jira automations that automatically route specific types of tickets to Rovo Dev agents for one-shot resolutions based on previous "reflections."
- Continuous learning: Discover how Rovo Dev gets better over time by storing reflections about your specific repository and team processes.

snippet.title: Why PMs who can't build will get left behind | Elena Verna | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
Elena Verna is Head of Growth at Lovable, one of the fastest-growing AI-native companies. She's previously held growth and product leadership roles at Dropbox, Miro, Amplitude, and SurveyMonkey, where she built some of the most influential frameworks in product-led growth.

We discuss
- The shift from "product manager" to "product builder" and why interviews now require working prototypes
- Automating Growth 101 work so you can focus on creative strategy
- The collapse of the talent stack: how roles in product, design, and engineering are blurring
- Three things that won't change: customer interaction, vision setting, and understanding distribution
- The "superpower framework" for career-accelerating decisions

Key takeaways
- PMs who can't build are becoming obsolete. The shift isn't theoretical or five years away. Top tech companies are already changing their interview processes to require functional prototypes instead of case studies. If you can't translate your product thinking into something tangible, you're competing with one hand behind your back.
- Automate Growth 101, then invest the freed-up time in creative strategy. The repetitive mechanics of growth marketing (A/B tests, funnel analysis, campaign setup) are increasingly automatable with AI. Elena argues that the PMs who thrive will be the ones redirecting that time toward the harder, more creative work that machines can't do yet.
- The talent stack is collapsing, and that's exciting. Boundaries between product, design, and engineering are blurring as AI gives individuals more autonomy across disciplines. Elena sees this as liberating rather than threatening. The PMs who embrace building, not just specifying, can move faster and validate ideas without waiting for a team to assemble.
- Three foundations won't change, no matter how good AI gets. Customer interaction, vision setting, and understanding distribution remain irreplaceably human. AI can accelerate execution, but it can't replace the judgment that comes from sitting with customers, setting a compelling direction, or knowing how your product actually reaches people.
- Your superpower lives at the intersection of what you're good at and what you love. Elena's career accelerated when she stopped trying to be well-rounded and started leaning into product-led growth as her defining skill. Find that intersection, then make career moves that compound on it rather than scattering your energy across unrelated opportunities.

snippet.title: How Cisco cut costs and made reporting 40x faster with Atlassian Cloud
snippet.description:
Cisco Networking, the world’s largest networking business unit inside Cisco, was drowning in fragmentation:

- 70+ Jira Data Center instances
- ~75 other tools
- Legacy work management and spreadsheets everywhere

In this customer story, Cisco leaders share how they partnered with Atlassian to consolidate 75+ systems into a single AI‑enabled Atlassian Cloud System of Work—and what it took to do so at enterprise scale.

With Atlassian Cloud Enterprise, Rovo, Confluence, Jira, Bitbucket, Xray, Forge, and Advisory Services, Cisco Networking has:

- Cut annual tooling costs by 54%
- Reinvested ~40% of OpEx back into the business within three years
- Accelerated program management reporting by up to 40x
- Made weekly status reporting ~24x faster
- Shifted 30% of engineering time from troubleshooting to innovation
- Unified 15,000+ users on a single Atlassian cloud platform

You’ll learn how Cisco:
- Turned a mandated exit from a legacy tool into a chance to redesign their System of Work
- Standardized taxonomy and workflows across hardware and software teams
- Replaced static PowerPoints with live Jira + Confluence dashboards for real‑time executive reporting
- Used Atlassian Rovo and Forge to build AI‑powered agents and custom apps that cut 10‑hour tasks down to 15 minutes
- Partnered with Atlassian Advisory Services to design cloud architecture, de‑risk migration, and manage change at scale

Read the full Cisco Networking story: https://www.atlassian.com/customers/cisco

snippet.title: Webinar Replay: Work Smarter, Not Harder: 3 Ways To Use AI to Stand Out at Work
snippet.description:
Stop being the busiest person in the room! Here’s how to get recognition for your AI-driven work.

You’re using AI to move faster, produce more, and check off tasks at an impossible pace—but why doesn't that extra output translate to the recognition you deserve? If you're a high-performer wondering how to stand out in the AI-driven workplace, you're not alone. Speed and output alone no longer guarantee visibility, recognition, or career growth.

In this virtual event from Atlassian's Team Playbook and Teamwork Lab, we're tackling the gap between effort and recognition. Learn why doing "more with AI" can quietly hurt your career, and discover three proven strategies to increase your visibility and drive clear, visible impact.

We walk through a simple Start, Stop, Keep framework for using AI intentionally. Find out how to use AI to:

- Sharpen your goals to achieve impact, not just output.
- Create AI working agreements to boost team collaboration and visibility.
- Treat AI as a thought partner to strengthen, not replace, your thinking.

If you're ready to move beyond using AI just to get more done and want to actually support your career growth, this video is for you.

Speakers & Experts:
- Lauren McGoodwin (Host) — Team Playbook Manager at Atlassian.
- Alisa Yu — Behavioral Scientist from Atlassian's Teamwork Lab. She oversees a group of researchers who use data and experiments to study teams, future work, and human-AI collaboration.
- Ben Ostrowski — Lead Behavioral Scientist for the Teamwork Lab. He designs research to answer key questions about how teams can collaborate most effectively with AI. The Teamwork Lab focuses on creating thought-leadership content on data-driven best practices for modern work.
- Amber Mory Woo (Guest) — Atlassian’s OKR Subject Matter Expert, who shares real-world examples of how she uses AI to set and achieve goals.

Resources & Next Steps:
- Atlassian Team Playbook: A free resource with research-backed exercises ("plays"), including AI-specific ones like the AI Working Agreements and AI Teammate Agent, designed to help teams solve work challenges. https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook 
- AI Collaboration Report & Quiz: Discover your AI collaboration style and find more insights on leading and innovating with AI. https://www.atlassian.com/blog/ai-collaboration-report-2025

localized.title: Webinar Replay: Work Smarter, Not Harder: 3 Ways To Use AI to Stand Out at Work
localized.description:
Stop being the busiest person in the room! Here’s how to get recognition for your AI-driven work.

You’re using AI to move faster, produce more, and check off tasks at an impossible pace—but why doesn't that extra output translate to the recognition you deserve? If you're a high-performer wondering how to stand out in the AI-driven workplace, you're not alone. Speed and output alone no longer guarantee visibility, recognition, or career growth.

In this virtual event from Atlassian's Team Playbook and Teamwork Lab, we're tackling the gap between effort and recognition. Learn why doing "more with AI" can quietly hurt your career, and discover three proven strategies to increase your visibility and drive clear, visible impact.

We walk through a simple Start, Stop, Keep framework for using AI intentionally. Find out how to use AI to:

- Sharpen your goals to achieve impact, not just output.
- Create AI working agreements to boost team collaboration and visibility.
- Treat AI as a thought partner to strengthen, not replace, your thinking.

If you're ready to move beyond using AI just to get more done and want to actually support your career growth, this video is for you.

Speakers & Experts:
- Lauren McGoodwin (Host) — Team Playbook Manager at Atlassian.
- Alisa Yu — Behavioral Scientist from Atlassian's Teamwork Lab. She oversees a group of researchers who use data and experiments to study teams, future work, and human-AI collaboration.
- Ben Ostrowski — Lead Behavioral Scientist for the Teamwork Lab. He designs research to answer key questions about how teams can collaborate most effectively with AI. The Teamwork Lab focuses on creating thought-leadership content on data-driven best practices for modern work.
- Amber Mory Woo (Guest) — Atlassian’s OKR Subject Matter Expert, who shares real-world examples of how she uses AI to set and achieve goals.

Resources & Next Steps:
- Atlassian Team Playbook: A free resource with research-backed exercises ("plays"), including AI-specific ones like the AI Working Agreements and AI Teammate Agent, designed to help teams solve work challenges. https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook 
- AI Collaboration Report & Quiz: Discover your AI collaboration style and find more insights on leading and innovating with AI. https://www.atlassian.com/blog/ai-collaboration-report-2025

snippet.title: Playbooks in Jira Service Management: Resolve work faster with guided, automated steps
snippet.description:
Playbooks in Jira Service Management help teams resolve incidents, service requests, and operational tasks faster by bringing clear, step-by-step guidance directly into the issue.

In this video, you’ll learn how playbooks:
- Provide in-context, actionable checklists so agents always know what to do next
- Combine instructional steps with automation to reduce manual work and context switching
- Improve consistency, auditability, and compliance across repeatable processes

You’ll also see how different roles use playbooks:
- On-call agents/responders – follow playbooks while working on issues, running automation steps, and tracking progress in execution logs
- Project admins/team leads – create and manage playbooks in space settings, translate existing processes into reusable templates, and target them with JQL so they appear in the right context

Finally, we walk through:
- How playbooks appear on a work item and how agents execute them
- How to configure steps (instructional vs. automation) and define where playbooks show up
- How templates and third-party automation actions help teams get started quickly
- Plan and feature requirements to start using playbooks

snippet.title: Rovo Dev Prompts in IDE | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Save it once, reuse it forever. ⚡

In this video, we walk you through the Prompts feature in Rovo Dev inside the IDE. Prompts let you quickly reuse common commands and workflows, so you don’t have to remember or retype your favorite instructions every time.

With Rovo Dev prompts, you can:
- Run /prompts to see a list of all commands you can instantly action
- Use the built-in, out-of-the-box prompts that ship with Rovo Dev
- Quickly reuse your saved prompts by typing /prompts and selecting the name from the list
- Create and save new prompts tailored to your own workflows

In the demo, you’ll see:
- How /prompts works inside the IDE
- How to pick and run an existing prompt from the list
- How to create a custom prompt, including one to optimise implemented changes before committing

If you often repeat the same kinds of tasks—like code optimisation before commits, refactoring patterns, or test workflows—Rovo Dev prompts help you standardise and speed up those actions with just a few keystrokes.

snippet.title: Rovo Dev YOLO Mode in the IDE | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Skip the prompts, ship the code. ⚡

In this video, we walk you through YOLO mode in Rovo Dev, available directly in your IDE. YOLO mode removes friction from the permission flow, so you can move faster while still staying inside your developer tools.

With YOLO mode in Rovo Dev, you can:
- Let Rovo Dev run commands automatically without confirming each permission
- Speed up repetitive actions like commits and other routine commands
- Stay in flow instead of constantly stopping to click “Allow.”

In the demo, you’ll see:
- How to enable YOLO mode from Preferences at the bottom of the Rovo Dev chat in your IDE
- How Rovo Dev behaves when YOLO mode is off (asks for approval before running commands)
- How it changes when YOLO mode is on (commits proceed automatically, no extra confirmation)

If you’re a developer who lives in the IDE and wants less friction in your AI-assisted workflow, YOLO mode is one of the most powerful ways to streamline your experience with Rovo Dev.

👉 Get started with Rovo Dev: https://www.atlassian.com/rovo-dev

snippet.title: Rovo Dev Plan Mode in IDE | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Plan first, code smarter. 

In this video, we show you how to use Plan Mode in Rovo Dev inside VS Code. Plan Mode helps you generate deep, structured implementation plans before you start coding, so you can tackle complex work with confidence.

With Rovo Dev Plan Mode, you can:
- Turn it on via Preferences at the bottom of the Rovo Dev chat in VS Code
- Ask for a step-by-step plan for complex features (like advanced security/auth flows)
- Get a detailed, multi-section plan with clearly described steps in each part
- Receive additional options and follow-ups you can choose to add to the plan

In the demo, you’ll see:
- How to enable Plan Mode in the IDE
- How Rovo Dev responds to a prompt like: “Give me a plan on how we can implement a complex security auth for this app.”
- How the generated plan is structured into sections with actionable steps

snippet.title: Cemre Güngor: How to ship AI features users actually use | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
Cemre Güngor has helped shape how billions interact with technology, from Facebook and Instagram's global sharing experiences to Figma's AI-powered workflows, and now reimagining the browser at The Browser Company with Dia.

In this conversation, we break down:
- Product Craft in the AI Era
- Why starting with the end in mind matters more than ever when prototyping is democratized
- The difference between durable AI features and "demo candy"
- How to evaluate prototypes without clear problem definition
- Scaling Products Across Surfaces
- What changes (and what doesn't) when building for social platforms vs creative tools vs AI-native workflows
- Why product managers get too attached to their existing mental models
- The hidden costs of ignoring new interaction paradigms
- Real AI Workflows at The Browser Company
- Practical examples: automated communication audits, personality type predictions, and workflow optimization
- Why meeting transcripts are the most underutilized data source in remote work

Jira Product Discovery is the home for all your product ideas, customer feedback, and bets, so you can prioritize what actually matters and share living roadmaps with your stakeholders. Turn scattered requests and spreadsheets into a single, shared source of truth that connects directly to delivery in Jira. Get it free at https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/product-discovery

10:50 Learning by doing and shipping quickly
14:39 How LLM-based features change product development
16:59 The Browser Company's focus on design and intentionality
19:10 The single most important test for an AI feature: internal usage

23:03 The Bitter Lesson: When to wait for model improvements

26:12 The necessity of shipping first to learn what good looks like for general-purpose AI assistants

32:47 The key value of an AI browser: bringing in your context

snippet.title: Aakash Gupta: The Skill Every Product Manager MUST Learn in 2026 | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
What if you could build product prototypes in 15 minutes instead of 3 weeks?

In this masterclass, Aakash Gupta (creator of the Product Growth Newsletter and former VP of Product at Affirm, Epic Games, and ThredUp) reveals the AI prototyping workflow that's revolutionizing product management.

Watch as he live-demos building a sleep tracker app using Bolt, V0, and Lovable, showing you exactly how to go from concept to a working prototype in minutes.

What You'll Learn:
- The 6-step framework every PM needs to master AI product building
- How to use Bolt, V0, Lovable & Cursor for rapid prototyping
- Why AI prototyping is the most significant change product management has ever seen
- Real-time demo: Building a sleep score calculator from scratch
- The exact prompt engineering techniques that get better results
- How to iterate across multiple AI tools to find the best output

The Four-Step AI Prototyping Method:
- Start with problem discovery (not jumping straight to solutions)
- Test across multiple tools (Bolt, V0, Lovable)
- Iterate with detailed feedback
- Move to Cursor for final refinements

"What used to take weeks now takes literally minutes." This isn't hype; this is the new reality for product builders.

About Aakash Gupta: Long-time product leader at ThredUp, Epic Games, Affirm, and Apollo. He now runs the Product Growth Newsletter (Substack), featuring practical playbooks and AI experiments for product builders.

snippet.title: Store Docker images in Bitbucket with Bitbucket Packages | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
In this video, I’ll show you how to store your Docker images directly in Bitbucket using Bitbucket Packages, so your code, CI/CD, and container images all live in one place.

Bitbucket Packages is a native Docker registry for Bitbucket. By keeping your images alongside your repositories and pipelines, you can reduce tech stack complexity and enhance your security posture by managing permissions in a single system, rather than juggling yet another external registry, such as Docker Hub or Artifactory.

You can also learn more about Bitbucket Packages by reading this blog: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/bitbucket/bitbucket-packages-container-registry

and reading this Atlassian support page: https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/getting-started-with-packages/

snippet.title: Bitbucket Pipelines Advanced Configuration Options | Bitbucket Blitz | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Unlock the full potential of your Bitbucket Pipelines! In this video, I introduce four advanced configuration options you can add to your bitbucket-pipelines.yml file to boost performance and cut costs:

- Size parameter for right-sizing compute per step

- Variable sharing for seamless state management

- Conditional step execution for smarter pipelines

- Flexible failure strategies to keep builds moving

Try adding a larger Size parameter to your slowest steps, or set up retry conditions for flaky tests to get started.

You can learn more about these advanced configuration options here: https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/step-options/

Discover Atlassian's Rovo Dev Code Reviewer, an AI-powered agent designed to transform your code review process!

In this video, we introduce you to Rovo Dev and demonstrate how it can make your code reviews faster, more consistent, and less manual.

Once enabled for your Jira or Bitbucket Cloud site, Rovo Dev automatically reviews your pull requests within minutes of creation. It analyzes your code, highlights potential issues, and suggests actionable improvements, helping you catch bugs early, enforce coding standards, and boost overall code quality.

Watch as we walk through a real example, showing how Rovo Dev reviews changes, leaves comments, and identifies areas for improvement, even catching intentional mistakes! Whether you're a developer, tech lead, or anyone involved in code reviews, Rovo Dev is a game-changer, especially for teams aiming to speed up reviews, reduce bottlenecks, and maintain high standards across large or distributed teams.

Rovo Dev supports both Bitbucket Cloud and GitHub, making it a versatile tool for modern development teams.

snippet.title: Introducing Rovo Dev in Jira | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
Take your Jira workflows to the next level with AI-powered sessions, now seamlessly integrated with Rovo Dev in the cloud.

In this video, we’ll show you how Rovo Dev in Jira transforms the way you manage and deliver work—combining the intelligence of Rovo Dev CLI with the convenience of Jira and the power of your IDE.

What’s a Session?
Rovo Dev in Jira is a self-contained, AI-driven workflow that helps you tackle Jira work items with unprecedented efficiency. Manage multiple sessions at once, each tailored to your specific tasks, and let the Rovo Dev Agent understand your context, coding standards, and project requirements.

Key Highlights:
- Instantly start Rovo Dev from any Jira work item with a single click
- Select the right repository and provide custom context for your agent
- Configure branch names and source branches with ease
- Generate code, review changes, and iterate, all within a dedicated session
- Track work item status and see all your sessions, their outputs, and progress in one place
- Effortlessly create pull requests and see them automatically linked to your Jira work items
- Interact with the agent: tweak, interrupt, or guide it via chat for maximum control

See It in Action:
Watch as we walk through a real-world example, starting from a Jira work item, launching a session, generating code, reviewing changes, and creating a pull request.

Experience how Rovo Dev brings the power of your IDE to Jira, making your development process smarter and more autonomous.

Want to learn more?
Check out our full How-To series playlist for more tips and deep dives:

snippet.title: Laura Burkhauser: Building AI habits that ship | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
Laura Burkhauser is CEO at Descript, where she's building AI-powered video editing tools that are changing how creators work. She's previously led product at Twitter, Rent the Runway, and The Tote. She's recognized for launching Underlord, Descript's AI co-editor, and expanding what's possible in creator productivity.

Key takeaways:
Don't lead with fear, lead with excitement. Rather than being driven by FOMO and the "burning platform" of AI disruption, discover your "beach moment" - something that genuinely excites you about AI's potential. For Laura, it was successfully shipping an undo button to production using Cursor and Claude. Once you experience that superpower feeling, investing in learning becomes natural.

Start with simulate, then automate, then delegate. Avoid immediately purchasing AI tools or attempting to automate everything. Begin by simulating workflows manually to validate the concept (as Laura did with post-launch tasks). Then build or purchase automation once you've proven it works. Finally, delegate when the system is dependable enough to run with minimal oversight.

Context is the new currency for career advancement. Junior employees previously earned their way into key meetings by creating slides or taking notes - tasks AI now handles. Today's juniors must identify new ways to provide value that leverage their AI-native abilities, gaining access to the context that will make them strategic leaders.

AI won't replace creativity; it amplifies it. In creative workflows, AI isn't about delegation - it's about achieving things you never thought possible. Laura went from creating 30-second clips to producing 30-minute videos. The objective isn't to hand off creative work, but to give creators superpowers to execute their vision more quickly.

Get your whole team to vibe code something. Laura required everyone on her product team to set up Cursor and prototype something they'd wanted to build but couldn't justify resources for. Once designers could handle their own VQA and PMs could ship features independently, the team was fully bought in. The experience of power drives adoption.

localized.title: Laura Burkhauser: Building AI habits that ship | Product in Practice
localized.description:
Laura Burkhauser is CEO at Descript, where she's building AI-powered video editing tools that are changing how creators work. She's previously led product at Twitter, Rent the Runway, and The Tote. She's recognized for launching Underlord, Descript's AI co-editor, and expanding what's possible in creator productivity.

Key takeaways:
Don't lead with fear, lead with excitement. Rather than being driven by FOMO and the "burning platform" of AI disruption, discover your "beach moment" - something that genuinely excites you about AI's potential. For Laura, it was successfully shipping an undo button to production using Cursor and Claude. Once you experience that superpower feeling, investing in learning becomes natural.

Start with simulate, then automate, then delegate. Avoid immediately purchasing AI tools or attempting to automate everything. Begin by simulating workflows manually to validate the concept (as Laura did with post-launch tasks). Then build or purchase automation once you've proven it works. Finally, delegate when the system is dependable enough to run with minimal oversight.

Context is the new currency for career advancement. Junior employees previously earned their way into key meetings by creating slides or taking notes - tasks AI now handles. Today's juniors must identify new ways to provide value that leverage their AI-native abilities, gaining access to the context that will make them strategic leaders.

AI won't replace creativity; it amplifies it. In creative workflows, AI isn't about delegation - it's about achieving things you never thought possible. Laura went from creating 30-second clips to producing 30-minute videos. The objective isn't to hand off creative work, but to give creators superpowers to execute their vision more quickly.

Get your whole team to vibe code something. Laura required everyone on her product team to set up Cursor and prototype something they'd wanted to build but couldn't justify resources for. Once designers could handle their own VQA and PMs could ship features independently, the team was fully bought in. The experience of power drives adoption.

snippet.title: Ravi Mehta: Data-driven prototyping with AI | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
Ravi Mehta is a senior product executive with experience leading product organisations at TripAdvisor, Facebook, and Tinder. He's the co-creator of Reforge's AI Strategy Program and currently works as a full-time product strategy adviser and investor with consumer brands and fast-growing startups.

Key takeaways:
AI generates the average - and that's both its strength and limitation. Large language models are trained on existing data, which means they excel at producing "pretty good" results quickly. But exceptional products aren't average - they're outliers. The goal isn't to move faster towards average solutions, but to use AI's speed to iterate rapidly towards something truly exceptional for your users.

Product work is splitting into human-speed and AI-speed activities. Understanding customers, creating a strategy, and building adoption happen at human speed. Writing documentation, creating prototypes, and increasingly design work happen at AI speed. The most successful product managers will focus on human-speed activities - customer discovery, product sense, and strategy - because these are where you add unique value.

The emphasis is shifting from craft to taste. Creating things used to require both taste (knowing what to build) and craft (the ability to build it). AI is democratising craft across creative fields. When anyone can generate beautiful designs or working prototypes, taste becomes the primary differentiator. For product managers, determining what to build becomes 90% of success, up from roughly 50% before.

Data-driven prototyping unlocks more sophisticated testing. Rather than starting with specifications or designs, begin with the data schema that will drive your experience. Generate mock data (or pull from existing systems), then ask AI to create an interface around that data. This creates better separation between presentation and data layers, makes iteration faster, and produces more realistic prototypes for user testing.

Three cohorts exist in every organisation: evangelists, interested learners, and sceptics. Evangelists are already experimenting daily. Interested learners need access and education to get started. Sceptics need to understand that whilst AI won't fulfil all the hype, it's genuinely transformative. People who refuse to engage with AI tools will fall behind in pace - not because AI replaces them, but because they're moving slower than necessary.

snippet.title: Kene Anoliefo: How to build context libraries and raise AI fluency | Product in Practice
snippet.description:
Kene Anoliefo has led product and design at Google, Spotify, and Netflix. She founded Heard, an AI-powered user research platform, and is now building tools that help teams capture and structure institutional knowledge so both people and AI can produce consistently high-quality work.

We discuss:
- The three Ps of AI adoption: people, process, and platform
- Why most companies jump to platform tools whilst ignoring the people problem
- Moving from gatekeepers to architects in product organisations
- Context enablement: turning implicit knowledge into explicit AI inputs
- The coordination tax and how AI changes team collaboration
- Why AI is like a brilliant but clueless new team member
- Building context libraries to 10x your AI output quality

Key takeaways:
Start with people, not platform tools. Most companies rush to buy AI tools whilst ignoring the deeper questions: Who am I in this AI era? What makes me valuable when AI can do parts of my job? Anxiety about AI is rooted in identity, not technology. Address the people layer first - help your team understand their evolving roles - before investing in new platforms.

Transform from gatekeepers to architects. Don't own user research, product strategy, or design - architect the principles and standards so anyone can do great work in those domains. With AI giving everyone superpowers, your value shifts from creating scarcity to enabling abundance. Make it an explicit team goal to help others do work that used to require specialists.

Context is your competitive advantage, not just data. AI trained on generic internet data produces generic output. Context libraries - structured repositories of your product strategy, design principles, customer segments, and research standards - help AI understand how your company specifically builds products. The investment in documenting this context has a multiplier effect on output quality.

AI is brilliant but clueless without your context. Think of AI as a talented new hire who needs onboarding. It has incredible capabilities but no understanding of your product, customers, or how your team works. Just like you'd explain these things to a new employee, you need to explicitly provide this context to AI tools through documentation optimised for machine reading.

Don't wait for permission to engage with AI. The biggest barrier isn't technical knowledge - it's mindset. You don't need to have worked at ML-first companies or taken AI courses. The cure for AI anxiety isn't trying to learn everything; it's starting with work you already love and asking how AI can make it 10-20% better. Focus on one thing, see results, then expand.

snippet.title: Team '25 Europe | Embarking on cloud with a security-first mindset
snippet.description:
Security isn’t just a checkbox in the cloud—it’s your biggest advantage. In this fast-paced 45-minute session, Atlassian’s Chief Information Security Officer kicks things off with a behind-the-scenes look at how we bake security into everything we build. Then, hear from our Head of Product, Information Protection, with a forward-looking vision of what’s next—from Customer-managed keys to isolated deployments and global compliance features—designed to keep your business resilient, compliant, and in control. We’ll wrap with a fireside chat featuring Chandra Bendarapu from Dailmer Truck AG, to unpack real-world strategies for securing data, scaling safely, and staying ahead of evolving threats.

Key takeaways:
- Gain insight into Atlassian’s evolving product security strategy to support global compliance and resilience at scale.
- Learn what's coming next in cloud security, including customer-managed keys, isolated deployments, and advanced compliance features designed to meet enterprise needs.
- Hear firsthand how Daimler Truck AG approached cloud security with Atlassian and —from migration planning to implementation—and the lessons they learned along the way.

snippet.title: Team '25 Europe | How Stellantis is driving innovation with the System of Work
snippet.description:
How does a 100-year-old global automotive company align 16 brands, thousands of employees, and complex organisational needs under one unified way of working? For Stellantis, it began with a strategic partnership, one that brought together their long-standing use of Atlassian tools and a shared vision for scaling smarter, more connected work.

In this session, Thomas Gärtner, Director of Software Integration Platform, and Chris Davidson, Principal Solutions Engineer, share how Stellantis and Atlassian co-created a System of Work roadmap tailored to their structure and goals, powered by the entire System of Work. Attendees will get an inside look at the experience of shaping this journey — from evaluating needs to building internal momentum, to what’s next as Stellantis rolls out their System of Work at scale.

Key takeaways:
- What large enterprises can learn from Stellantis’ early-stage alignment, stakeholder engagement, and approach to enterprise-scale transformation
- Equip participants with insights needed to effectively navigate the transition from legacy systems to innovative solutions
- How Stellantis tailored a System of Work roadmap by developing a long-term vision for innovation, strategic partnership with Atlassian and AWS, and a deep discovery process

snippet.title: Team '25 Europe | Iterating at scale: How AirFrance-KLM grows their System of Work
snippet.description:
For Air France-KLM, migrating to Atlassian Cloud wasn’t the finish line — it was just the beginning. The journey unfolds in several stages: first, making the move to the Cloud. Next, fully benefit from its capabilities. Then, continuously adjust and optimise their instance for greater efficiency. And finally, strategically leverage the evolving functionalities available in the Cloud.

In this session, moderated by Windy Goodale (Sr. Strategic Customer Success Manager at Atlassian), Jordy Essed (DevNet Team Product Owner) and Hicham Ouali (DevNet Team Scrum Master) share how Air France-KLM views their System of Work as a long-term, evolving journey. They’ll discuss the mindset and practices behind continuous improvement —emphasizing collaboration between business and technology, iterative rollout strategies, and lessons learned from scaling in a large, complex organisation. Whether you’re just beginning or looking to deepen your journey, this session provides an inside look at how progress, value, and impact unfold over time.

Key takeaways:
- Why Cloud migration is just the first step in a much broader transformation
- How to realise ongoing value through optimisation and adoption of new capabilities
- Practical insights for fostering sustainable, organisation-wide change

snippet.title: Discover Atlassian's new home in Bengaluru | Atlassian
snippet.description:
We invited YouTuber and MarkItUp founder, @IshanSharma7390, to take you on a tour of Atlassian's brand-new Bengaluru office - where innovation, collaboration, and community come together to shape the future of work in India!

From humble beginnings to what's now a thriving community of nearly 2,300 Atlassians, with over 1,100 based in Bengaluru, this new space is more than just an office. It's where some of India's top R&D talent come together to build the future of human-AI collaboration.

Spanning approximately 200,335 square feet (equivalent to about four football fields), our state-of-the-art workspace is designed for the future of distributed work.

Discover:
- 420+ ergonomic workstations and 200 agile work settings
- 70 collaboration studios and a 280-seat café
- A five-room, 250-seat ITG centre for events and learning
- Multipurpose sports courts for cricket, pickleball, badminton, and more
- Two lush, landscaped terraces and over 10,800 plants - bringing Bengaluru's "garden city" spirit indoors

At Atlassian, we believe in fostering connection through thoughtful design, food, and events. Whether you're collaborating in a studio, brainstorming in a private nook, or recharging in our green spaces, you'll find an environment built to help you do the best work of your life.

snippet.title: Streamline your code reviews with automated acceptance criteria checks | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
In this video, we explore how the Code Reviewer feature can enhance your pull request workflow by automatically analyzing your code against acceptance criteria from linked work items.

Watch as we demonstrate how Code Reviewer scans your pull request and the associated ticket—checking the summary, description, and custom fields to ensure all requirements are addressed.

You'll see a clear, actionable report right in your pull request, showing:
- Which acceptance criteria have been met
- Which are missing
- Which may need manual review

This makes it easy to ensure your changes fully satisfy the requirements before merging!

Tips for Success:
- Follow best practices for writing acceptance criteria
- Include the ticket ID in your branch names or commit messages for optimal results

In this demo, we use Rovo Dev CLI to generate a ticket and acceptance criteria, then intentionally leave some criteria incomplete to show how Code Reviewer highlights gaps.

You'll see how this process helps developers catch issues early, reduce back-and-forth, and deliver higher-quality work with confidence.

Check out the Atlassian Community Forum post for more tips: https://go.atlss.in/ivp3tp 

👉 Get started with Rovo Dev: https://www.atlassian.com/rovo-dev

snippet.description:

What you’ll learn:
- What sessions are and how they help you keep context, memory, and history across commands
- How to create a new session with /sessions new
- How to list all your available sessions with /sessions
- How to rename your current session for better organization
- How to restore previous sessions and pick up right where you left off
- How to clear messages in your current session with /clear
- How to prune a session to reduce token size while keeping essential context
- How to fork a session to branch off a line of work

- Maintain continuity across complex tasks and conversations
- Easily switch between different projects or work streams
- Keep your workspace organized and relevant to your current focus
- Branch off new ideas or tasks without losing previous context

snippet.title: Set up custom code review standards with Rovo Dev CLI | Rovo Dev | Atlassian
snippet.description:
In this video, we'll walk you through how to set up your own custom code review standards using the Rovo Dev CLI.

With code reviewer customization, your team can enforce unique coding standards across all pull requests, helping you catch issues early and maintain high-quality code.

What you’ll learn:
- How to create a .rovodev folder and a .review-agent.md file in your repo
- How to describe your team’s code review standards in natural language
- How to use Rovo Dev CLI and AI to generate comprehensive code review guidelines (covering performance, code quality, security, naming conventions, and more)
- Tips for writing clear, actionable standards and excluding non-critical formatting feedback
- How to generate synthetic code violations to test your standards and see the code reviewer in action
- How to update your custom instructions with good and bad code examples for even better results

Whether you’re an engineering leader or a developer looking to improve your team’s code quality, this step-by-step guide will help you get started with automated, customizable code reviews.

snippet.description:

What you’ll learn:
- What shadow mode is and why it’s useful for developers and teams
- How to enable shadow mode using the --shadow flag
- How shadow mode simulates actions and provides outputs without modifying your code, repositories, or external systems
- How to preview the effects of commands, validate automations, and demonstrate workflows risk-free

- Safely test commands and automations before applying them
- Audit and review potential changes without impacting your projects
- Demonstrate workflows and train team members in a risk-free environment

snippet.title: How the Aurora Education Foundation uses Jira to empower student success | Atlassian Foundation
snippet.description:

In this video, you’ll learn:
How nonprofits can use Jira for program planning and tracking
Tips for onboarding teams and scaling new tools
Real-world outcomes and advice for organizations exploring Jira

snippet.title: Migrate to Bitbucket Pipelines from Jenkins | The Developer's Edge | Atlassian
snippet.description:
In this video, we briefly discuss developer experience before diving into the details of setting up and running a simple CI/CD system using Jenkins and AWS EC2.

Using tightly integrated, cloud-native products like Bitbucket Pipelines provides a better developer experience than using self-hosted on-prem tools like Jenkins.

With self-hosted on-prem, developers spend less time building software and solving problems for their customers and more time maintaining their on-prem software.

We also examine a few features of Bitbucket Pipelines, such as Dynamic Pipelines, that improve the developer experience and can save teams significant amounts of money.
